newsitem.title: USA: Scientists delighted with U.S. shuttle flight.
newsitem.headline: Scientists delighted with U.S. shuttle flight.

text.p: As the crew of space shuttle Columbia neared the end of a 16-day research mission, scientists said on Monday they were delighted with the results so far.
"We're in the home stretch, there's no doubt about it," said Mission Scientist Michael Robinson. "Things are going very, very well. The science teams are happy and they're also very exhausted."
Since blasting off on July 1, Columbia's crew of seven has been working around the clock in two shifts to complete a $86 million programme of scientific research.
The astronauts have sparked 197 fires as part of their combustion research, many more than planned.
"Things have been just great. I don't know how else to say it," Robinson said.
Columbia has enough supplies to stay in orbit an extra day, but NASA officials said they were not considering extending the flight.
"We're looking forward to wrapping up the mission," Lee Briscoe, mission operations director, said.
The shuttle is to return to earth at the Kennedy Space Centre shortly after sunrise on Thursday. Weather conditions were expected to be favourable for the shuttle's landing.

Columbia's crew beamed down pictures of a small dent in one of the shuttle's cabin windows, thought to be caused by space debris. Similar damage has occurred on shuttle flights before and is not considered serious.
